newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to deregulate oil product exports in July.
newsitem.headline: Japan to deregulate oil product exports in July.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Monday it will deregulate oil product exports in July, two months earlier than originally planned.
Starting July 1, oil firms and trading houses will be free to set export prices of their oil products, an official for MITI's Agency of Natural Resources and Energy said.
Previously, they were not allowed to set prices substantially different from levels in the domestic market.

The official also said that starting July 14 oil product exporters will need permission for exports just once a year, and can ship their products overseas as many times as they like as long as their accumulated export volume is within the approved figure.
Currently, they need to get permission from the agency each time they plan to export oil products.
Oil firms in Japan have largely been inactive in product exports as cumbersome and time-consuming application processes make it difficult for them to conduct timely export operations.
It usually takes one week or more to gain government approval under the current system, but during that time overseas market conditions may have totally changed, oil product traders said.
Japan's oil product imports were liberalised in April 1996, and expectations of cheaper gasoline imports put a downward pressure on retail gasoline prices, squeezing refiners' profit margins.
MITI previously said it planned to deregulate oil product exports by September.
